The 340 K kinetic threshold is Editorial judgement (Kerotakis): the blue-to-black conversion on warming is qualitative in every source we have, so the number is a stated stand-in for a rate we do not model, not a measurement

M from IUPAC/CIAAW atomic weights on the same basis as the other sulfates here (S 32.065, O 15.9994); modelled as concentrated aqueous acid, as HCl is. Dilution heat NOT curated, and for this acid that is a real omission rather than a rounding one: diluting concentrated sulfuric acid releases roughly 95 kJ/mol, which is the whole reason for 'add acid to water'. The bench will not warm the beaker, so it cannot teach that lesson yet

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(s), density: standard reference values. The reagent a permanganate titration is standardised against, and the cleanest way to put a reducing agent in the beaker
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. The reduced half of the couple school electrochemistry is built on
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. The oxidised half; whether iron is here or as Fe(II) is what a redox experiment measures

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. Copper(I): unstable in water on its own — it disproportionates — but a real part of the distribution a coupled solve finds, and present here so that copper which settles into it is counted rather than dropped

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. The reduced manganese the databases book dissolved Mn as; its faint pink is why a permanganate titration endpoint is read on the purple going, not on anything arriving

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. Manganese(VI): the deep green intermediate between permanganate and manganese dioxide, and a real minor product of permanganate in alkali — it exists here so that manganese which settles into this state is counted rather than quietly lost
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights. Manganese(III), which the databases carry and a coupled solve can land a little of matter in; present so that it is counted

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; colour curated, strength set from the published molar absorptivity of MnO4- (ε ≈ 2400 L/mol/cm at 525 nm) — visible at 1e-5 M, which is why it is the classic titration indicator

M from IUPAC/CIAAW atomic weights; an acid-base indicator, so its colour is not a property of the substance but of the pH around it — see kerotakis_core::indicator, which carries the pKa and both forms' spectra
M from IUPAC/CIAAW atomic weights; sodium salt, freely soluble; colour is pH-dependent — see kerotakis_core::indicator
M from IUPAC/CIAAW atomic weights; colour is pH-dependent — see kerotakis_core::indicator
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; ion Cp not modelled (see module docs)

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(s), density: standard reference values; dissolution enthalpy -80.4 kJ/mol derived from NBS/Wagman 1982 formation enthalpies (ZnSO4(s) -982.8, Zn2+(aq) -153.9, SO4 2-(aq) -909.3 kJ/mol)
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(g): standard reference values

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(s), density: standard reference values. NOT flagged as a toxic metal: the L0 screen has no class for that, so lead is as unremarked here as sodium chloride, which is wrong about the world and is written down rather than hidden
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; ion Cp not modelled (see module docs)

M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; density standard reference. Dissolution enthalpy +35.4 kJ/mol derived from NBS/Wagman 1982 formation enthalpies: Pb(NO3)2(s) -451.9, Pb2+(aq) -1.7, NO3-(aq) -207.4 kJ/mol, so -1.7 + 2(-207.4) + 451.9 = +35.4. Calorimetric values around +33.6 are also quoted; the 2 kJ/mol spread is the disagreement between the two routes and is not resolved here. Cp(s) 145 is an ESTIMATE from the nitrates' range, not a sourced value, and nothing computed depends on it while the salt is dissolved
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(l) 81.1 J/(mol.K) and density 0.7914 g/mL at 25 C: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed.
M from IUPAC/CIAAW 2021 atomic weights; Cp(l) 195.6 J/(mol.K) and density 0.6606 g/mL at 25 C: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 97th ed.
